title: The crushing of the heart and the path to glory
english: "...that the man's heart shall be lifted up." The proud man hears words against pride, and at times he experiences the trial of afflictions, seeing that he is blinded. If you fall by this crushing, which leads you more effectively through the pains concerning humility, the heart is not lifted up. Before the rebuke—so that I may speak thus—and before the lashes, he has a lifted-up heart. For when he falls through afflictions, he recognizes that because of his own pride he has fallen down to the thoughtless.

Thus it must be heard also regarding: "Capernaum, which until heaven you were lifted up, shall be brought down to Hades" (Luke 9:79). And to be brought down to Hades is a crushing. Before this crushing, he had been proud. "Before glory, one is humbled" (Proverbs 18:12). It is necessary first to be humbled voluntarily, so that one may attain glory; for second, glory comes after the un-blinding. For this reason also the Savior said: "The one humbling himself will be lifted up" (Luke 14:11). And behold, "everyone lifting himself up will be humbled" (Matthew 23:12); he will be crushed here. Before this crushing, he has a lifted-up, vainglorious, proud heart.

Again, glory is brought to the one humbling himself, so that he may be un-blinded. Before this glory, it is necessary to be humbled; it is necessary to work, so that he may receive a reward. Therefore, he receives glory of the un-blinding from God. In this way also Peter exhorts, saying: "Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that you may be lifted up in due time" (1 Peter 5:6). And Job indeed says: God is the one "making the humble into height" (Job 22:9).

And "crushed" here he says "the heart," not those whose hearts are harmed. And sometimes the name of the crushing signifies such a thing as not having healthy thoughts, not having straight understandings. This crushing of the heart needs a physician, and a physician who heals what is hidden; for it has been said: "The Lord builds Jerusalem and gathers the dispersals of Israel, he who heals the crushed in heart" (Psalm 147:2).
